by: Filing Flows reading of the 10-K (every figure from the filing's XBRL; see the checks)
summary: Revenue rose 65% to $215.9B and the balance sheet nearly doubled to $206.8B, but the notes show where the growth is being financed and stored: inventories more than doubled to $21.4B with $95.2B of supply commitments behind them, private and public equity stakes jumped from $3.8B to $40.0B, and $14.4B of goodwill arrived with the Groq licence.

Every total in the statements ties to its note. The gaps that remain are explained differences: the Groq consideration still owed explains most of why accrued liabilities rose $4.4B more than the cash flow statement shows, buybacks booked exceed cash paid by $0.3B, and $9.0B of other income is mostly unrealized gains on equity stakes that never touched cash.

threads.title: Groq: $13.0B in cash, $3.9B still owed, $16.9B on the balance sheet
threads.text: The December 2025 licence and hiring deal was paid $13.0B at closing (the investing line "Groq, Inc.") with $4B, including imputed interest, due within a year — carried at $3.9B as "accrued purchase consideration" in accrued liabilities, up from $9M. It was recorded as $14.4B of goodwill (Compute & Networking; goodwill now 10% of assets against 5%) and a $2.5B developed-technology asset with a five-year life. That asset is why next year's intangible amortization is $923M against $488M this year, and why accrued liabilities rose $9.6B while the cash flow statement's accrued line shows $5.3B: about $3.9B of the gap is consideration not yet paid.

threads.title: Other income of $9.0B is mostly paper gains on stakes
threads.text: Other income, net was $9.0B (6.4% of pretax income) against $1.0B. The notes account for nearly all of it: $6.6B of unrealized gains on publicly held equity securities and $2.4B of upward adjustments on private stakes, less $0.1B of impairments. The cash flow statement takes $8.9B of investment gains back out of operating cash flow, and the deferred tax liability on equity investments rose from $0.3B to $2.2B. $10.5B of the public stakes are locked up for now and $4.8B are locked up until December 2027 (held in other assets).

threads.title: Inventory and supply: the build-up behind the growth
threads.text: Inventories rose 112% to $21.4B against revenue up 65% — work in process from $3.4B to $8.8B and finished goods from $3.3B to $8.8B — covering 125 days of cost of revenue against 113. Provisions charged to cost of revenue were $4.0B (a year earlier $1.6B) and the accrual for purchase obligations in excess of demand rose to $2.7B. Behind the balance sheet are $95.2B of manufacturing, supply and capacity commitments, 4.4 times inventory and substantially all due in fiscal 2027. The cash flow statement's inventory line (−$11.3B) matches the balance sheet change to within $1M, so none of the increase came from acquisitions.

threads.title: Warranty doubled with rack-scale systems
threads.text: The warranty liability went from $1.3B to $2.8B: $2.5B of additions (1.15% of revenue, against 0.92% a year earlier) and $1.0B used. The additions relate primarily to Compute & Networking. The same $2.8B appears in accrued and other current liabilities, so the liability is all current.

threads.title: Customers pay ahead, and a few of them matter a lot
threads.text: Two direct customers bought 22% and 14% of revenue, and three hold 56% of receivables (25%, 18%, 13%). Receivables are 65 days of revenue, as a year earlier. Deferred revenue rose to $2.6B: $11.1B of additions, $9.0B of them customer advances, against $10.4B recognized ($8.9B from advances) — customers are prepaying for supply.

threads.title: Taxes: a higher rate, and more of it under review
notes: Schedule II - Valuation and Qualifying Accounts
threads.text: The effective rate rose to 15.1% from 13.3%: the deduction for foreign-derived income (−3.0 points) and Israel's reduced rate (−2.2 points) still pull it below 21%, but the benefit from stock compensation shrank to −1.0 point from −2.5. Cash taxes were $20.3B against $22.8B of current tax, so taxes payable rose ($0.9B → $2.7B current; $2.2B → $4.0B long-term). Unrecognized tax benefits grew to $4.4B, $2.0B of it from this year's positions. A $711M release of state valuation allowances is most of Schedule II's $873M deduction.

threads.title: Capital return: buybacks plus the shares withheld at vesting
threads.text: The equity statement books $40.4B of repurchases (282M shares) against $40.1B paid in cash — trades not yet settled and the 1% excise tax account for the $0.3B. Another $7.9B went to taxes on vested awards, paid by withholding 51M shares, which exceeds the $6.4B of stock compensation and is why paid-in capital fell. The share count fell 173M to 24.3B (160M issued, 51M withheld, 282M bought back); diluted EPS of $4.90 recomputes from net income and shares.

threads.title: Leases and cloud capacity not yet on the balance sheet
threads.text: Operating lease liabilities are $2.9B, but $22.7B of data-center leases are signed and not yet commenced (7.7 times today's liability), plus $27B of multi-year cloud service commitments — $7B of it next year. Both support research and development and will move onto the balance sheet or through operating costs over the next several years.

threads.title: Debt: small, and about to shrink
threads.text: $8.5B of notes ($8.47B net); the $1.0B 3.20% notes due 2026 moved to short-term debt ($999M), which ties to the balance sheet. Interest expense of $259M is 3.1% of average debt. The commercial paper programme was raised from $575M to $25.0B with nothing outstanding.

notes.Segment Information: Compute & Networking earned a 67% segment margin on $193.5B (+67%); Graphics 41% on $22.5B (+57%). By market, Networking grew fastest (+142% to $31.4B) and Data Center is 90% of revenue. Revenue is now by customer headquarters: the U.S. is 69% ($149.6B), China fell 21% to $19.7B, and NVIDIA estimates 76% of Data Center revenue from Taiwan-headquartered customers went to end customers in the U.S. and Europe. Long-lived assets in Taiwan more than doubled to $3.2B; the split by region ties to property and equipment of $10.4B.
notes.Stock-Based Compensation: Stock compensation was $6.4B (3.0% of revenue); $14.8B of unearned compensation will be recognized over about 2.3 years. The RSUs and PSUs that vested were worth $22.2B at vesting against about $5.7B at grant (146M units at $39.14) — withholding taxes are paid on the vesting value.
notes.Cash Equivalents and Marketable Securiti: Cash, equivalents and marketable securities total $62.6B; $39.5B are debt securities, about half maturing within a year. Cash equivalents of $8.3B within cash of $10.6B leave about $2.3B in bank deposits.
notes.Income Taxes: Gross deferred tax assets rose to $16.9B, led by the tested-income asset (+$2.6B), while the capitalized-research asset fell from $6.3B to $5.4B.
